findings: The existing arithmetic-preserving norm optimization retains exact scientific results at K64 and K65 with one/seven threads, including K65 low memory.

The baseline fast one-FE median rises from 0.403 to 7.297 seconds at one thread and 0.182 to 2.457 seconds at seven threads between K64 and K65. ADR0012 retains columnwise moments and QR above 64 finite candidates.
The supplemental captures are sequential diagnostic runs, not alternating confirmation pairs; their before/after timings are not additional speedup claims.
The original paired K50 speedup claim and its source/artifact bindings were independently rechecked; its historical receipt remains unchanged.

independent_oracle.method: explicit group elimination and independent NumPy SVD least squares; analytic IID covariance

limits: No production change beyond the existing norm optimization.
No F0 screen, qualification, SCC, Windows run, solver-policy change or installed-plugin replacement.
Existing multi-FE exact-repeat failures and incomplete reference records in the original receipt remain open.
next_step: Profile the K64/K65 finite-solve boundary and prepare a bounded all-width guarded-solve proposal with memory and rank evidence before requesting any ADR0012 policy change.
